[Judy Blume](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Judy_Blume "Judy Blume") is the author featured most frequently on this list (five times). Her [young adult novels](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Young_adult_fiction "Young adult fiction") are typically about [coming of age](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Coming_of_age "Coming of age") issues such as teenage sexuality.

[![Image 5](https://thumb.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/5/5d/J._K._Rowling_2010.jpg/250px-J._K._Rowling_2010.jpg?utm_source=en.wikipedia.org&utm_campaign=parser&utm_content=thumbnail)](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/File:J._K._Rowling_2010.jpg)

The _[Harry Potter](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Harry\_Potter "Harry Potter")_ series by [J. K. Rowling](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/J._K._Rowling "J. K. Rowling") was the most challenged work from 2000 to 2009. Its focus on [witchcraft](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Witchcraft "Witchcraft") has generated [controversy](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Religious_debates_over_the_Harry_Potter_series "Religious debates over the Harry Potter series").

[![Image 6](https://thumb.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/e/ef/Mark_Twain_life_1900s.jpg/250px-Mark_Twain_life_1900s.jpg?utm_source=en.wikipedia.org&utm_campaign=parser&utm_content=thumbnail)](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/File:Mark_Twain_life_1900s.jpg)

The second oldest works featured on the list were written by [Mark Twain](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mark_Twain "Mark Twain"). _[Adventures of Huckleberry Finn](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Adventures\_of\_Huckleberry\_Finn "Adventures of Huckleberry Finn")_ (1884) is often challenged for its language and discussion of racism.

This **list of the most commonly challenged books in the United States** refers to books sought to be removed or otherwise restricted from public access, typically from a [library](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Library "Library") or a school curriculum. This list is primarily based on U.S. data gathered by the [American Library Association](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/American_Library_Association "American Library Association")'s Office for Intellectual Freedom (OIF), which gathers data from media reports, and from reports from librarians and teachers.[[1]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/List_of_most_commonly_challenged_books_in_the_United_States#cite_note-1)

As of 2020, the top ten reasons books were challenged and banned included sexual content (92.5% percent of books on the list); offensive language (61.5%); unsuited to age group (49%); religious viewpoint (26%); LGBTQIA+ content (23.5%); violence (19%); racism (16.5%); drugs, alcohol, and smoking (12.5%); "anti-family" content (7%); and political viewpoint (6.5%).[[2]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/List_of_most_commonly_challenged_books_in_the_United_States#cite_note-2)[[3]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/List_of_most_commonly_challenged_books_in_the_United_States#cite_note-infographics-3)[[4]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/List_of_most_commonly_challenged_books_in_the_United_States#cite_note-:0-4)[_[better source needed](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Wikipedia:Verifiability#Questionable\_sources "Wikipedia:Verifiability")_]

[Judy Blume](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Judy_Blume "Judy Blume") is the author featured most frequently on this list (five times). Her [young adult novels](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Young_adult_fiction "Young adult fiction") are typically about [coming of age](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Coming_of_age "Coming of age") issues such as teenage sexuality.

[![Image 5](https://thumb.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/5/5d/J._K._Rowling_2010.jpg/250px-J._K._Rowling_2010.jpg?utm_source=en.wikipedia.org&utm_campaign=parser&utm_content=thumbnail)](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/File:J._K._Rowling_2010.jpg)

The _[Harry Potter](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Harry\_Potter "Harry Potter")_ series by [J. K. Rowling](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/J._K._Rowling "J. K. Rowling") was the most challenged work from 2000 to 2009. Its focus on [witchcraft](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Witchcraft "Witchcraft") has generated [controversy](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Religious_debates_over_the_Harry_Potter_series "Religious debates over the Harry Potter series").

[![Image 6](https://thumb.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/e/ef/Mark_Twain_life_1900s.jpg/250px-Mark_Twain_life_1900s.jpg?utm_source=en.wikipedia.org&utm_campaign=parser&utm_content=thumbnail)](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/File:Mark_Twain_life_1900s.jpg)

The second oldest works featured on the list were written by [Mark Twain](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mark_Twain "Mark Twain"). _[Adventures of Huckleberry Finn](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Adventures\_of\_Huckleberry\_Finn "Adventures of Huckleberry Finn")_ (1884) is often challenged for its language and discussion of racism.

This **list of the most commonly challenged books in the United States** refers to books sought to be removed or otherwise restricted from public access, typically from a [library](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Library "Library") or a school curriculum. This list is primarily based on U.S. data gathered by the [American Library Association](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/American_Library_Association "American Library Association")'s Office for Intellectual Freedom (OIF), which gathers data from media reports, and from reports from librarians and teachers.[[1]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/List_of_most_commonly_challenged_books_in_the_United_States#cite_note-1)

As of 2020, the top ten reasons books were challenged and banned included sexual content (92.5% percent of books on the list); offensive language (61.5%); unsuited to age group (49%); religious viewpoint (26%); LGBTQIA+ content (23.5%); violence (19%); racism (16.5%); drugs, alcohol, and smoking (12.5%); "anti-family" content (7%); and political viewpoint (6.5%).[[2]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/List_of_most_commonly_challenged_books_in_the_United_States#cite_note-2)[[3]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/List_of_most_commonly_challenged_books_in_the_United_States#cite_note-infographics-3)[[4]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/List_of_most_commonly_challenged_books_in_the_United_States#cite_note-:0-4)[_[better source needed](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Wikipedia:Verifiability#Questionable\_sources "Wikipedia:Verifiability")_]
